hypothesis: H0: High-NtB attrition contains meaningful contextual decisions. H1: HOLD becomes overwhelmingly dominant at high NtB.

analysis.verdict: H0 SUPPORTED — attrition auction is real but not degenerative
evidence: K=5: Hold chains up to 8 (mean 3.0) — multi-turn attrition auctions are real
K=5: Attack rate still 72.4% — HOLD is NOT overwhelmingly dominant even at K=5
K=5: 31.7% time in danger band — significant high-NtB gameplay exists
K=3: Max hold chain=4, mean=1.5 — meaningful attrition, reduced repetition
K=3: 19.1% danger time, 65.3% attack rate — good balance
K=1: Max hold chain=1, 47.1% attack rate — attrition eliminated, very cautious
First-player advantage: minimal (56-61% range, small sample)
design_implications: K=5 is NOT degenerative — the attrition auction creates real decisions
K=3 looks like the sweet spot — preserves meaningful attrition while reducing repetitive standoffs
K=1 removes too much strategic texture — not recommended
The 'intentional failure to hold NtB' mechanic is working as designed
caveats: Only 200 games per cell — need 1000+ for statistical confidence
First-player advantage inconclusive with this sample size
Need per-state decision density analysis (are decisions context-dependent?)
